sections.kicker: The agentic platform for AI-hybrid creative production
sections.title: From the first word to the final frame.
sections.lead: Write it, previsualise it, render it, review it, perform it — in one place, with a crew of agents, on every device.

sections.title: Every production lives in two worlds that never meet.
sections.lead: The real one: a stadium, a street, a ferry deck, a crew with cameras and LED walls. The virtual one: scripts, 3D, renders, AI. Today you hold them together by hand, with a dozen tools and a lot of meetings.

beats.title: Lost in translation
beats.text: A venue is measured once, then redrawn in every tool. By the time it reaches the stage, nothing quite matches.

beats.title: Waiting on each other
beats.text: Previs waits for the plan, the render waits for the previs, the client waits for the render. Every hand-off costs a day.

beats.title: No one holds the whole
beats.text: AI tools are brilliant and blind: no memory of the show, no idea what the stage or the camera look like.

sections.closing: What if the virtual world were not a copy, but a double: tied to the real one by data?
body: The result is a production where the creative intent is clear but the information is scattered. Nobody is doing it wrong; the tools simply do not share a world.

sections.title: The digital double.
sections.lead: A digital double is not a 3D model you export once. It is a living twin, tied to the real thing by data. Measure the real, mirror it in 3D, and from then on both move together.

points.title: 1 · Measure
points.text: Scans, plans, photos, LiDAR, maps: the real world becomes data, once.

points.title: 2 · Mirror
points.text: The same data drives a 2D plan and a 3D stage, side by side, always in step.

points.title: 3 · Move together
points.text: Change the double and the real follows: LED pixel maps, cameras, plates, cues. Change the real and the double updates.

body: Today a “model” is a snapshot: someone exports a file, someone else imports it, and from that moment it starts to drift from the real venue. A digital double is different. It is a living twin that stays tied to the real thing by data: dimensions, positions, cameras, screens, even the video playing on them.

In N’Brain the double is the project’s shared dataset, not a picture of it. The 2D plan, the 3D stage, the pixel map for the LED processor, the camera plates and the cues that run the show are all views of the same data. Edit one and the others change, because there is only one thing underneath.

That is why it works in both directions. Measure the real world (a scan, LiDAR, a map, a photo) and the double updates. Change the double (move a camera, recolour the wall, swap the clip) and the real world receives the exact numbers to follow: the pixel map, the lens, the cue. Real and virtual stop being two versions of the truth.
It also gives the AI something to hold on to. An agent that can see the stage, the camera and the shot makes useful decisions, instead of guessing from a text prompt.

sections.title: Three layers, because three jobs must never mix.
sections.lead: Fast things must never wait for slow things. So N’Brain separates where people and devices meet, where decisions are made, and where the truth is kept.

layers.title: Show control
layers.job: The one surface where people and devices meet.
layers.without: Every craft ships its own app, its own login, its own remote.
layers.proof: One workspace on desktop, tablet and phone. MIDI, OSC, gamepad, camera. Edit and Live in one tap.

layers.title: N’Brain
layers.job: Agents that read the show and act on it, through one tool surface.
layers.without: AI is a chat box with no memory, no stage and no gate.
layers.proof: A stage director per room. Approval at every gate. Typed decisions in about 20 ms.

layers.title: Knowledge & data
layers.job: The single source of truth: scripts, shots, takes, versions, the double itself.
layers.without: The truth lives in someone’s folder, in three versions.
layers.proof: Per-project memory. Lore version control. Every take filed on its shot.

sections.rule: The data plane (telemetry, cues, LED) never waits for an AI: no LLM in the hot path, sub-millisecond to two frames. AI explains and suggests; the rails stay deterministic.
body: Each layer does one job and talks to its neighbours only through a narrow, typed surface. People and devices at the top send intent down; agents turn intent into actions; the data layer records what happened and answers what is true. State and results flow back up.

The separation is what makes it fast and safe. Slow, creative, AI-driven work lives in the control plane: it can take seconds, ask for approval and be wrong. Live work (telemetry, cues, LED, cameras) lives on the data plane and never waits for a model. Neither can break the other.

It is also what makes it yours. The data sits on your machines and in your versions; the agents can drive local GPUs or cloud engines; the interface is just a browser. Upgrade one layer without rebuilding the others, work offline for 24 hours on a signed grant, or host everything in the cloud.
